commits.edited_message:
liblzma: Store used Record counts in Index groups

Change index_group.last from the index of the last Record to the number of Records in use. This simplifies size calculations when a group is optimized or duplicated.

Reject Number of Records values that cannot fit in the remaining input before decoding any Records.

liblzma: Preserve check statistics in lzma_index_dup()

lzma_index_dup() copied the per-Stream flags but not the cached bitmask for all Streams except the last one. Copy the cached bitmask too.

Also put the element size first in the Record copy calculations.

coupling: The first commit changes index_group.last from a zero-based last-record index to the number of used Records, and updates every consumer present at that commit. The later commit rewrites the Record copy arithmetic in lzma_index_dup(); with the original zero-based representation its srcg->last + 1 expressions are equivalent, so that commit is benign in isolation. When both edits are combined, srcg->last + 1 means one Record past the used-record count. index_dup_stream() allocates exactly src->record_count Records but copies one extra Record from every source group. A public index built with lzma_index_init(), 513 lzma_index_append() calls, and lzma_index_dup() has two groups (512 and 1 Records), so the second copy reads and writes past the allocated destination Record array. A correct repair must track the invariant across the two commits and update the coupled copy length and running offset together, or revert the representation change and consistently update the later index-tree consumers; a repair that addresses only one side of the count invariant leaves the copy loop inconsistent.
